answer: An attester must stake 20% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the grove stake is held until the willow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the copper audit lists each exposure. A farm running 101 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. That is 34 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
